usdRate.sourceName: Bank of Mauritius, consolidated indicative exchange rates
usdRate.note: Mid-point of the consolidated indicative USD buying (46.41, notes) and selling (47.99) rates on 30 October 2026; the BoM page showed 46.42/47.99 again on 3 November 2026.

inflation_cpi.sourceName: Statistics Mauritius CPI, September 2026, via Trading Economics
inflation_cpi.note: Year-on-year inflation 5.7% in September 2026 (4.9% in August), released by Statistics Mauritius on 7 October 2026; secondary source as the official release page was not reachable. The 12-month average headline rate was about 4.1%.

inflation_projection.sourceName: Bank of Mauritius inflation objective range 2-5%; 2026 forecast about 5%
inflation_projection.note: Planned at 4.5%, near the top of the central bank's 2-5% range, because the 2021-2025 average (about 5.8%) and the 2026 forecast (about 5%) sit above its midpoint.

policy_rate.sourceName: Bank of Mauritius, MPC media release 12 August 2026
policy_rate.note: Key Rate kept at 4.75% after a 25 bp rise on 20 May 2026; still shown as current on the BoM site on 30 October 2026.

savings_account_rate.sourceName: Bank of Mauritius, Monthly Statistical Bulletin August 2026, Table 17a (banks' interest rates on new rupee deposits)
savings_account_rate.note: Savings deposit rates ranged 3.15-3.65% in June and July 2026 (raised from 2.95-3.40% in May 2026 after the Key Rate rise); midpoint used. Interest on an individual's savings or fixed deposit is tax-exempt.

fdr_3m_rate.note: The BoM only publishes ranges by term band: new rupee time deposits up to 6 months ranged 1.25-4.35% in July 2026 (MSB August 2026, Table 17a), too wide to give a typical 3-month rate.

fdr_1y_rate.note: The BoM only publishes ranges: new rupee time deposits of 6-12 months ranged 0.55-4.70% and 12-24 months 3.25-4.70% in July 2026 (MSB August 2026, Table 17a); no typical 1-year rate is published.

dps_rate.note: No published rate for a standard monthly recurring deposit product was found in BoM statistics.

bank_deposit_avg_rate.sourceName: Bank of Mauritius, Monthly Statistical Bulletin August 2026, Table 18 (weighted average rupee deposits rate of banks)
bank_deposit_avg_rate.note: Weighted average rate on all rupee deposits of banks, 2.67% in July 2026 (includes low-rate savings and demand deposits). World Bank FR.INR.DPST gives 4.54% for 2025 on a different basis.

sanchayapatra_5y_rate.note: No retail Government savings bond is on sale: the last, the 3.5% Four-Year Government of Mauritius Savings Bond (prospectus at bom.mu), closed on 14 February 2025, and no 2026 issue was found.

tbill_91d_rate.sourceName: Bank of Mauritius, auction results of 91-day BOM Bills, 22 October 2026
tbill_91d_rate.note: Weighted average yield 4.30% (range 4.24-4.44%). These are Bank of Mauritius bills; Government Treasury bill yields were similar (91-day about 4.0% in August 2026).

tbond_5y_rate.sourceName: Bank of Mauritius, Monthly Statistical Bulletin August 2026, Table 40c (switch auction into the new 5.35% Five-Year Government of Mauritius Bonds)
tbond_5y_rate.note: Weighted yield 5.35% at the 19 August 2026 switch auction into the new 5.35% five-year benchmark bond; the 7 August 2026 switch into the 5.15% bond yielded 5.32%, and the last regular 5-year auction (20 May 2026) 4.99%.

tbond_10y_rate.sourceName: Bank of Mauritius, Monthly Statistical Bulletin August 2026, Table 40a (Ten-Year Government of Mauritius Bonds)
tbond_10y_rate.note: Weighted yield 5.60% at the 14 August 2026 auction of the 5.55% ten-year bond (5.62% in April 2026).

tax_bank_interest.note: Interest on a savings or fixed deposit account held by an individual with a bank or non-bank deposit-taking institution is exempt income (Income Tax Act, Second Schedule, Part II); other interest is taxed in income at 0%, 10% or 20%. The MRA page was unreachable on 3 November 2026 for re-checking; PwC Tax Summaries (deductions) lists this interest separately in the housing-relief income test, consistent with its exempt status.

tax_sanchayapatra_profit.note: No retail savings bond is currently on sale and the tax treatment of savings-bond interest is not stated in the last prospectus or on the MRA exempt-income page.

deposit_insurance_limit.sourceName: Bank of Mauritius, Mauritius Deposit Insurance Corporation FAQ
deposit_insurance_limit.note: Rs 300,000 per depositor per Scheme member, under the Mauritius Deposit Insurance Scheme Act 2019 operative from 14 June 2024; confirmed in the MDIC Annual Report 2024-2025.

credit_card_rate_cap.note: No legal cap was found; the BoM bulletin publishes card volumes but no credit card interest rate.

equity_return_low.sourceName: SEMDEX near 2,266 in July 2026, about 2,000-2,500 for most of the past decade
equity_return_low.note: Low case: the local market keeps its flat price record and investors earn mostly dividends.

equity_return_base.sourceName: SEMDEX 10-year record weak; safe after-tax rate about 4%
equity_return_base.note: Held 2.5 points above the roughly 4% tax-free deposit and bill rate because the SEMDEX price index has gained little in ten years and returns come mostly from dividends.

equity_return_high.sourceName: SEMDEX record high 2,530 (February 2025); global equity history
equity_return_high.note: High case: a diversified local and global equity fund with rupee depreciation lifting foreign returns.

gold_return_low.sourceName: Gold trend in dollars; rupee about 35 per dollar in 2016 and 47.2 in October 2026 (BoM)
gold_return_low.note: Low case: flat dollar gold prices with mild rupee depreciation.

gold_return_base.sourceName: Gold trend in dollars; rupee about 35 per dollar in 2016 and 47.2 in October 2026 (BoM)
gold_return_base.note: Base case: a long-run dollar gold trend of about 5% plus about 2.5% a year of rupee depreciation, its pace over the last decade.

gold_return_high.sourceName: Gold trend in dollars; rupee about 35 per dollar in 2016 and 47.2 in October 2026 (BoM)
gold_return_high.note: High case: strong gold years and faster rupee depreciation.

fixed_income_return_low.sourceName: BoM: 91-day bill 4.30% (22 Oct 2026), 364-day bill 4.32% and 10-year bond 5.60% (Aug 2026); bank 1-year deposits up to about 4.7%, interest on individuals' bank deposits tax-exempt (MRA)
fixed_income_return_low.note: Low case: savings accounts (about 3.4%) and short deposits after rate cuts.

fixed_income_return_base.sourceName: BoM: 91-day bill 4.30% (22 Oct 2026), 364-day bill 4.32% and 10-year bond 5.60% (Aug 2026); bank 1-year deposits up to about 4.7%, interest on individuals' bank deposits tax-exempt (MRA)
fixed_income_return_base.note: Base case: tax-free 1-year bank deposits and bills of about 4.0-4.3%, rounded down.

fixed_income_return_high.sourceName: BoM: 91-day bill 4.30% (22 Oct 2026), 364-day bill 4.32% and 10-year bond 5.60% (Aug 2026); bank 1-year deposits up to about 4.7%, interest on individuals' bank deposits tax-exempt (MRA)
fixed_income_return_high.note: High case: 5- to 10-year Government bonds at 5.3-5.6%, taxed at a low marginal rate.

life_claim_settlement_rate.note: The Financial Services Commission publishes long-term claims amounts by insurer but no industry claim settlement ratio was found.

insurance_term_premium_table.note: Term life cover is sold, but no regulator or official source publishes indicative premiums per Rs 1,000 of cover; only company quotes exist.

health_hospitalisation_cost.note: Public hospital care is free; no official figure for the out-of-pocket cost of a private hospital stay was found.

health_premium_table.note: No regulator or official source publishing private health insurance premiums by age was found.

oop_health_share.sourceName: World Bank WDI, out-of-pocket expenditure (% of current health expenditure), Mauritius
oop_health_share.note: 45.2% in 2023 (WHO Global Health Expenditure Database), the latest available; older than 2025.

goal_inflation_health.sourceName: Inflation assumption 4.5%; private health costs largely imported
goal_inflation_health.note: No separate medical price projection was found; private medical costs are planned 1.5 points above general inflation.

goal_inflation_education.sourceName: Inflation assumption 4.5%; education CPI up 6.3% year on year in September 2026 (Statistics Mauritius via Trading Economics)
goal_inflation_education.note: Public schooling is free, but education prices rose 6.3% in the year to September 2026, faster than the CPI, so education is planned 1 point above general inflation.

life_expectancy.sourceName: World Bank WDI, life expectancy at birth, total (SP.DYN.LE00.IN), Mauritius
life_expectancy.note: 73.8 years in 2024 (men 70.4, women 77.4), from Statistics Mauritius via the World Bank.

life_table_remaining.sourceName: UN World Population Prospects 2024 via populationpyramid.net
life_table_remaining.note: Secondary source of UN WPP 2024 (medium variant) for 2026; totals are the mean of men and women except at 65, where the page gives 17.4. The Statistics Mauritius 2021-2023 life table gives similar values (men 17.9, women 21.7 at 60-64).

support_ratio.sourceName: World Bank SP.POP.DPND.OL (2025); UN WPP 2024 via populationpyramid.net (2040, 2065)
support_ratio.note: Working-age people per person 65+, computed as 100 / old-age dependency ratio: 19.8 in 2025 (World Bank) gives 5.1; 32.0 in 2040 and 63.3 in 2065 (populationpyramid.net/mauritius/2040/ and /2065/) give 3.1 and 1.6.

retirement_age_default.sourceName: Workers' Rights Act 2019 (consolidated to Act 13 of 2026), section 2 and section 109, MRA
retirement_age_default.note: The Act defines retirement age as 65 and bars employers from requiring retirement earlier; the Basic Retirement Pension age is also rising to 65 for everyone turning 60 from 1 September 2029 (Finance Act 2025), so 65 applies to anyone born after 1975.

retirement_age_government.sourceName: News on Sunday (defimedia.info), Pension reforms: a bitter necessity
retirement_age_government.note: Secondary source: the civil service retirement age was raised gradually from 60 to 65; no official Pensions Act text was reachable. Older than 2025.

retirement_return_low.sourceName: BoM: 91-day bill 4.30% (22 Oct 2026), 364-day bill 4.32% and 10-year bond 5.60% (Aug 2026); bank 1-year deposits up to about 4.7%, interest on individuals' bank deposits tax-exempt (MRA)
retirement_return_low.note: Low case: savings accounts and short deposits.

retirement_return_base.sourceName: BoM: 91-day bill 4.30% (22 Oct 2026), 364-day bill 4.32% and 10-year bond 5.60% (Aug 2026); bank 1-year deposits up to about 4.7%, interest on individuals' bank deposits tax-exempt (MRA)
retirement_return_base.note: Base case: kept below the roughly 4% tax-free 1-year deposit and 364-day bill rate.

retirement_return_high.sourceName: BoM: 91-day bill 4.30% (22 Oct 2026), 364-day bill 4.32% and 10-year bond 5.60% (Aug 2026); bank 1-year deposits up to about 4.7%, interest on individuals' bank deposits tax-exempt (MRA)
retirement_return_high.note: High case: a ladder of 5- to 10-year Government bonds.

retirement_accumulation_return_low.sourceName: Safe rate about 4%; equity base 6.5%; gold base 7.5%
retirement_accumulation_return_low.note: Low case: mostly deposits and Government bonds.

retirement_accumulation_return_base.sourceName: Safe rate about 4%; equity base 6.5%; gold base 7.5%
retirement_accumulation_return_base.note: Base case: a balanced mix of bonds, deposits and equity funds.

retirement_accumulation_return_high.sourceName: Safe rate about 4%; equity base 6.5%; gold base 7.5%
retirement_accumulation_return_high.note: High case: a growth-leaning mix with local and global equity funds.

old_age_allowance_monthly.sourceName: Ministry of Social Integration, Social Security and National Solidarity, Basic Retirement Pension
old_age_allowance_monthly.note: Basic Retirement Pension of Rs 15,000 a month for ages 60-89 from January 2025, still the amount on the ministry page last updated February 2026; a Rs 15,555 figure in a July 2026 press article is only a reference pension used in projections, so no 2026 increase could be confirmed. Universal, no means test (the minister said the means test was abandoned, L'Express July 2026); to become the State Age Pension from 2027.

old_age_allowance_eligibility.sourceName: Ministry of Social Security, Basic Retirement Pension; Finance Act 2025 age schedule (L'Express via AllAfrica)
old_age_allowance_eligibility.note: BRP is paid to residents meeting residence rules (citizens under 70: 12 years since age 18) without a means test; its age rises from 60 to 65 in steps, reaching 65 for anyone turning 60 from 1 September 2029 (fr.allafrica.com/stories/202601090287.html), so 65 applies to anyone planning today. Ages 90-99 receive a higher rate (Rs 22,710 from January 2025).

gratuity_rule.sourceName: Workers' Rights Act 2019 (consolidated to Act 13 of 2026), section 109, MRA
gratuity_rule.note: Gratuity on retirement after 12 months' service: 15 days' remuneration per year of continuous employment, daily rate on 26 days a month; paid through the Portable Retirement Gratuity Fund for service since 2020, and the employer may offset part of an employer-funded pension.

public_pension_scheme.note: The contributory layer is in transition: National Pensions Fund contributions were replaced by the CSG in 2020, and Budget 2026-27 announced a new defined-contribution National Pensions Fund from 1 July 2027; its rules were not yet published. The universal Basic Retirement Pension is reported under old_age_allowance.

savings_account.note: Banks pay 3.15-3.65% (July 2026); interest is tax-exempt for individuals.

fdr_3m.note: Short fixed deposits are offered; the BoM only publishes rate ranges.

fdr_1y.note: One-year fixed deposits are offered, up to about 4.7% in July 2026.

dps.note: No standard monthly recurring deposit product with published rates was found.

sanchayapatra_5y.note: Retail savings bonds are issued from time to time through banks; the last (3.5%, four years) closed in February 2025.

tbill_91d.localNameEn: Treasury bills / Bank of Mauritius bills (91 days)
tbill_91d.note: Auctioned weekly by the BoM; individuals can buy through banks and primary dealers.

tbond_5y.note: Auctioned by the BoM; individuals can buy through banks and primary dealers or on the stock exchange.

tbond_10y.note: Auctioned by the BoM; individuals can buy through banks and primary dealers or on the stock exchange.

equity_fund.note: Collective investment schemes are licensed by the Financial Services Commission.

gold.note: The Bank of Mauritius sells gold coins to the public; gold bars are also sold.

insuranceComplaints.name: Office of the Ombudsperson for Financial Services
insuranceComplaints.note: Complaints about insurers go here after the insurer's own process; the FSC also explains complaints handling at fscmauritius.org/en/consumer-protection/complaints-handling.

pensionScheme.name: Ministry of Social Security (National Pensions Fund and CSG retirement benefits)
pensionScheme.note: A new defined-contribution National Pensions Fund is due from July 2027.

oldAgeAllowance.name: Basic Retirement Pension (Ministry of Social Security)
oldAgeAllowance.note: Universal pension; age rising from 60 to 65 by 2034; to be renamed State Age Pension from 2027.

publicHealthCover.name: Ministry of Health and Wellness (free public health care)

depositInsurance.name: Mauritius Deposit Insurance Corporation (via Bank of Mauritius)
